claims.text: A counter is a cumulative metric whose value only increases or is reset to zero on restart; http_requests_received_total is a counter (# TYPE ... counter).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Metric types (Counter); outputs/stage-2/scripts/devops/metrics-endpoint.txt (# TYPE line)

claims.text: A gauge is a single numerical value that can go up and down; http_requests_in_progress (prometheus-net, # TYPE gauge) is the number of requests currently in progress in the pipeline.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Metric types (Gauge); live /metrics @ stage-2 (HELP/TYPE of http_requests_in_progress); prometheus-net README

claims.text: OrderMetrics.cs@stage-2:5-14 defines donhang_orders_placed_total via Metrics.CreateCounter; OrdersController.Create (and OrdersV2Controller) call if (created) OrderMetrics.OrdersPlaced.Inc(); a repeated Idempotency-Key returns the earlier order and does not increment.
In a PromQL selector, label="v" matches equal values and label=~"re" matches values against a regular expression (fully anchored), so code=~"5.." selects codes 500-599 and code=~"4.." codes 400-499.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Querying basics (instant vector selectors, label matchers =, =~; RE2, fully anchored)

claims.text: A bare metric name as a query selects every series of that metric.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Querying basics (instant vector selectors)

claims.text: rate(v[5m]) returns, per series, the per-second average increase over the last 5 minutes and needs at least two samples in the window; counter resets (drops) are adjusted, so the result is never negative; rate is for counters only (a gauge's drops would be read as resets).
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Query functions, rate(); Metric types (counter reset)

claims.text: sum by (code) (expr) sums the input series, grouping by the code label, and the result keeps only the code label.
claims.source_hint: Prometheus docs: Operators, aggregation operators (sum, by)

claims.text: Series of http_requests_received_total differ by code, method, controller, action and endpoint (plus job and instance added by Prometheus).
Prometheus adds the labels job and instance (the target's host:port, here api:8080) to scraped series.

promql-rate.sh@stage-2 output: two 201 for POST with the same new Idempotency-Key, counter up by 1; code=~"4.." query returns only the 404 series; sum by (code) returns {code=200} and {code=404}; rate(donhang_orders_placed_total[5m]) returns one series with instance and job.

The script's helpers: place_order POSTs /api/v1/orders with the current key, orders_placed reads donhang_orders_placed_total from api:8080/metrics, promql queries prometheus:9090/api/v1/query and prints labels => value.

Metrics.CreateCounter registers the counter in prometheus-net's default registry; the static field is initialised on first use of OrderMetrics (first new order), so before that /metrics has no donhang_orders_placed_total line.

Try it: the script places two test orders (three POSTs: one so the counter exists, then two with one new key), sends 10 requests for product 1 (200) and 3 for product 999 (404), sleeps 11 s (two scrapes at 5 s), prints the output shown.
